o: Count how many characters of s equal letter, multiply by 100, divide by len(s), rounding down. Example 1: 2/6 → 33. Example 2: 0/4 → 0. Constraints are tiny (|s| ≤ 100), so a direct count is all that is needed; integer division naturally floors the result.
k: Integer division (count * 100) // len(s) performs the required floor automatically.
No floating point needed — avoid precision issues entirely.

a.i: Use the built-in count of the target character, scale by 100, and floor-divide by the string length.
s: Count occurrences of letter in s.

w: Single approach suffices. Pitfall: doing floating-point division then flooring can produce 32.99999 → 32 due to representation error; keep it in integers. Follow-up: none meaningful — this tests basic fluency.
